bullets: Game 2 of 4 in a Hero-Berserker deck-showcase video (readable window 176.3-454.5s): the X-Bow 2.9 shell with Rocket in the spell slot and Fire Spirit where most lists run Archers, introduced as "trying out the hero berserker with X-Bow… the hero berserker is pretty strong in siege decks" (t=177-185). Won it in triple-elixir overtime with the enemy right tower at 354 HP — "Very nice win, dude. This berserker is just ridiculously strong" (t=449-452).

The loop is one X-Bow per elixir tier, one row or three off the river ([13, 12] at clock 2:19, [14, 12] at 1:24, [13, 12] at 0:57, [2, 12] at 0:50, [4, 12]/[14, 14]/[15, 12] in overtime), never tanked by a big unit: the Hero Berserker at the bridge plus Savage Survival is the tank, and Tesla, Electro Spirit, Fire Spirit, Skeletons and The Log are the screen.

Savage Survival is used three times as a defender-clearer, never for tower damage (it does -75% to Crown Towers): clock 2:15 to wipe the defence off the first X-Bow ("It's going to completely wipe out everything… Look at that Tesla. Oh my god. It's already gone"), clock 0:42 "just to win the one-v-one" against an Evo Tesla, and overtime 0:43 against the opponent's own Hero Berserker.

Against a Golem list whose only real X-Bow answer is the Rocket, the deck is played as an elixir tax: pre-emptive bridge Teslas at clock 1:36 and 0:57 and a 2-elixir Berserker at 1:22 to force the Rocket — "this is basically just guaranteeing him have to defend with the rocket, which is really good for us" (t=270-273) — then a fresh X-Bow behind it.

The Rocket slot is what the Fireball version does not have: held until overtime, then two casts at [12, 22] for 342 HP each on the enemy right tower, on the theory that "he's going to have to start rocket cycling us back. And once he starts rocket cycling, I think we'll be able to break through pretty simply, just by going expo plus berserker and the ability" (t=353-361).

Skeletons and Tesla are also used as predictions rather than reactions late on — Skeletons pre-placed for the Miner (t=335, 391) and a Tesla dropped to beat the opponent's Tesla ("let's go with Tesla to predict his Tesla. Perfect", t=415-419).

new_deck.rationale: X-Bow is the win condition and every other slot is a 1-4 elixir answer that protects it or cycles back to it, with Rocket as the closer.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The standard X-Bow 2.9 cycle with **Rocket** instead of Fireball and a **Fire Spirit** in the Archers slot, built around the **Hero Berserker** as the bridge tank. Because Savage Survival makes her undestroyable for four seconds, a 2-elixir card next to a fresh X-Bow clears whatever the opponent drops on the building — Ryley's pitch is that defending a siege building normally means putting cards at the bridge, and this deck punishes exactly that: "you can just instantly wipe out their defenses and they just don't have enough elixir to kind of recoup". Tesla doubles as a defensive pull and as pre-emptive X-Bow armour at the bridge, which leaves an opponent with only a heavy spell as a real answer. Rocket then converts that into a win condition of its own: once the enemy has to spend Rocket on every X-Bow, Ryley rockets the tower back for free damage and wins the cycle race in overtime.
